question: Which company's mascot is the Michelin Man, also called Bibendum?
explanation: 'Michelin Man' gives away the answer Michelin. The text also reveals 'Bibendum', which is the answer to entry 18.
fix: Change the text to "Bibendum, a mascot made of white tyres, represents which company?" and drop entry 18 as a duplicate.

question: Which chocolate brand is famous for the slogan “Have a break, have a KitKat”?
explanation: The slogan contains the brand name, so the answer is given away.
fix: Change the text to "Which chocolate bar's long-running slogan is “Have a break, have a ...”?"

question: Which advertising slogan ends with “...because you're worth it”?
explanation: The question asks for a slogan, but the options are brands. It also asks the same fact as entry 19 and Parts entry 28.
fix: Change the text to "Which cosmetics brand uses the slogan “Because you're worth it”?" and drop entry 19.

question: Which brand's long-running advertising character is the Energizer Bunny?
explanation: The character's name contains the brand name.
fix: Change the text to "A drumming pink bunny that 'keeps going and going' advertises which battery brand?"

question: The “Just Do It” slogan is associated with Nike.
explanation: This is the same fact as entry 2 ('Which brand is associated with the slogan “Just Do It”?'), and it also appears in Parts entry 28.
fix: Drop, or replace it with a different true/false fact, e.g. "The Energizer Bunny began as a parody of a rival battery brand's bunny." (true; it parodied the Duracell bunny in 1989). Do not use the 1988 debut year: entry 23 already asks it.

question: What is the name of the Michelin Man's official mascot character?
explanation: The answer, Bibendum, is printed in entry 4's question. The wording is also circular: the Michelin Man is the mascot, and Bibendum is his name.
fix: Drop (consistent with the entry 4 fix).

question: Which brand's slogan is “Because I'm worth it” or “Because you're worth it”?
explanation: This is the same fact as entry 8 (L'Oréal slogan).
fix: Drop.

question: What is the name of the cartoon character used to advertise Kellogg's Frosted Flakes?
explanation: This is the same fact (Tony the Tiger and Kellogg's) as entry 7, and it is repeated in Pairs entry 29.
fix: Drop, or replace it with another mascot, e.g. "What is the name of the leprechaun mascot of Lucky Charms?" (Lucky / Lucky the Leprechaun).

question: What is the name of the advertising campaign that used the phrase “Where's the beef?”
explanation: The accepted answer is the phrase quoted in the question. Entry 12 also already covers the 'Where's the beef?' ad.
fix: Drop as a near-duplicate of entry 12, or rewrite as "Which actress delivered the line “Where's the beef?” in Wendy's 1984 ads?" with accepted ["Clara Peller", "Peller"] and then rework entry 12 (whose answer is Wendy's elderly customer, i.e. Peller).

question: Which artist painted the album cover for the Beatles' Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band?
explanation: The cover was not painted. It is a photographed collage tableau designed by Peter Blake and Jann Haworth and shot by Michael Cooper.
fix: Change text to "Which British pop artist co-designed the album cover for the Beatles' Sgt. Pepper's Lonely Hearts Club Band?"

question: Which actress was the first woman to win an Academy Award for Best Director?
explanation: Kathryn Bigelow is a director, not an actress. Calling her an 'actress' is misleading and may lead players to rule her out.
fix: Change text to "Who was the first woman to win the Academy Award for Best Director?"

question: Dolly Parton co-wrote the song 'I Will Always Love You'.
explanation: Dolly Parton wrote 'I Will Always Love You' (1973) alone; there is no co-writer. The marked answer true depends on the word 'co-wrote', which is false.
fix: Change text to "Dolly Parton wrote the song 'I Will Always Love You', later a hit for Whitney Houston." and keep answer true.

question: Keanu Reeves was born in Canada.
explanation: Keanu Reeves was born in Beirut, Lebanon (1964) and grew up in Toronto. He is Canadian, but he was not born in Canada.
fix: Set answer to false, or change text to "Keanu Reeves was born in Beirut, Lebanon." with answer true.

question: What is the surname of singer-songwriter Taylor Swift?
explanation: The answer is in the question, so the question is trivial and meaningless.
fix: Drop, or replace it with "Which singer-songwriter's 2023-24 Eras Tour became the highest-grossing concert tour ever?" (Taylor Swift).

question: Which comedian created and starred in the sitcom Seinfeld?
explanation: The sitcom's title gives the answer away. Also, Seinfeld was co-created with Larry David.
fix: Change text to "Which comedian co-created the sitcom Seinfeld with Jerry Seinfeld but rarely appeared on screen?" with accepted ["Larry David", "David"].

question: Match each actor with a film they directed.
explanation: The Kevin Costner / Dances with Wolves pair asks the same fact as entry 8 ('Which actor directed the film Dances with Wolves?').
fix: Replace the Costner pair with e.g. "Ben Affleck" / "Argo".

question: What is the real name of the Marvel hero Black Panther?
explanation: T'Chaka, a distractor, is T'Challa's father and also held the Black Panther mantle in the comics and films, so it is defensibly correct. N'Jadaka (Killmonger) also takes the mantle in the 2018 film.
fix: Replace distractors "T'Chaka" and "N'Jadaka" with "W'Kabi" and "Zuri" (keep M'Baku).

question: Which artist co-created the comic character Hellboy?
explanation: Mike Mignola is credited as Hellboy's sole creator, so 'co-created' is inaccurate. Pairs entry 30 also lists Mignola under 'a character they co-created'.
fix: Change "co-created" to "created". In entry 30, change the text to "Match each comic creator with a character they created or co-created."

question: What is the name of the newspaper photographer who is often Spider-Man's rival?
explanation: J. Jonah Jameson is the publisher and editor-in-chief of the Daily Bugle, not a photographer. The Bugle's photographer is Peter Parker himself.
fix: Change text to "What is the name of the Daily Bugle publisher who constantly attacks Spider-Man in print?"

question: How many issues were in the original 12-issue comic series Watchmen? Give the number of issues.
explanation: The question states '12-issue', which gives away the answer 12.
fix: Change the text to "How many issues were in the original Watchmen comic series? Give the number of issues."

question: Which phrase is strongly associated with the “Distracted Boyfriend” meme?
explanation: The correct answer is identical to the meme name in the question, and the distractors are other meme names rather than phrases, so the question means nothing.
fix: Drop, or rewrite as "The 'Distracted Boyfriend' meme originated as what kind of image?" with the answer 'A stock photo'.

question: What is the name of the meme featuring a man pointing at a butterfly and asking if it is a pigeon?
explanation: The description 'asking if it is a pigeon' gives away the answer 'Is This a Pigeon?'.
fix: Change the text to "What is the name of the meme in which an anime character misidentifies a butterfly?"

question: Which video game character dances in the “Harlem Shake” viral video trend?
explanation: The question assumes a false premise. The Harlem Shake trend has no video game character, so the 'correct' answer is a non-answer and the distractors make no sense.
fix: Drop, or replace it with "The 2013 'Harlem Shake' trend used a track by which producer?" with Baauer as the correct answer.

question: Which viral 2012 campaign encouraged people to dump ice water over themselves for ALS awareness?
explanation: The Ice Bucket Challenge went viral in summer 2014, not 2012.
fix: Change "2012" to "2014" in the text.

question: What is the name of the meme in which a dog sits calmly in a burning room?
explanation: The accepted list includes "Gunshow", which is the name of KC Green's webcomic, not the meme. It is also the same fact as part 2 of entry 28 (dog in a burning room = This Is Fine).
fix: Remove "Gunshow" from accepted. Then drop this entry or drop the 'Dog in a burning room' part from entry 28.

question: What is the name of the viral dance trend performed to “Harlem Shake”?
explanation: The answer, 'Harlem Shake', appears in the question.
fix: Drop, or rewrite as "Which 2013 viral dance trend starts with one masked person dancing alone before the whole room erupts?" with Harlem Shake accepted.

question: Order these viral internet phenomena by when they first became famous, earliest first.
explanation: Rickrolling (4chan, May 2007; mainstream in 2008) and Charlie Bit My Finger (uploaded May 2007, viral 2007-08) became famous at essentially the same time, so their relative order is debatable.
fix: Replace "Charlie Bit My Finger" with "Leeroy Jenkins" (2005), giving the order Dancing Baby, Leeroy Jenkins, Rickrolling, Gangnam Style. (Nyan Cat, 2011, also works but entry 27 already orders Dancing Baby before Nyan Cat.)

question: What is the name of the electronic handheld game with a character called Simon that repeats light patterns?
explanation: The question names 'Simon', which is the answer. Simon is the game itself, not a character in it.
fix: Change the text to "Which 1978 electronic game has four coloured buttons that light up in sequences players must repeat?"

question: What puzzle cube was invented by Hungarian architect Ernő Rubik?
explanation: The inventor's name gives the answer away ('Rubik' -> Rubik's Cube). The same fact also appears in Pairs entry 30.
fix: Change the text to "Which puzzle, invented in Hungary in 1974 by an architecture professor, is now the world's best-selling puzzle toy?" and remove "Magic Cube" from accepted; or keep the proposed 'originally sold as the Magic Cube' wording but then "Magic Cube" must be removed from accepted.

question: What spring toy became famous for walking down stairs?
explanation: This is the same fact (Slinky) as entry 7, and Slinky also appears in Pairs entry 30.
fix: Drop, or replace it with another toy, e.g. "What toy, launched by Wham-O in 1958, is a plastic ring swung around the waist?" (Hula Hoop).

question: What word game was invented by Alfred Mosher Butts?
explanation: This is the same fact (Butts and Scrabble) as entries 28 and 29.
fix: Keep this entry and resolve the duplication there: drop entry 28 and remove the Scrabble pair from entry 29 (see their fixes).

question: How many wooden blocks are in a standard 54-block Jenga tower? Give the number of blocks.
explanation: '54-block' gives away the answer 54.
fix: Change the text to "How many wooden blocks are in a standard Jenga set? Give the number of blocks."

question: How many letter tiles are in the standard English-language Scrabble set? Give the number of tiles.
explanation: The standard set has 100 tiles: 98 letter tiles plus 2 blanks. Asking for 'letter tiles' makes 98 defensible.
fix: Change "letter tiles" to "tiles (including blanks)" and keep answer 100.

question: Put these board games in order of first commercial release, earliest first.
explanation: Milton Bradley's The Checkered Game of Life was released in 1860, before Monopoly (1935), so 'The Game of Life' could go first. The listed order assumes the 1960 version.
fix: Replace "The Game of Life" with "Trivial Pursuit" (1981), giving Monopoly (1935), Cluedo (1949), Risk (1957), Trivial Pursuit (1981).

question: Name the two classic board games designed by Alfred Mosher Butts and Anthony E. Pratt, respectively.
explanation: Both parts repeat entry 29 (Scrabble / Butts and Cluedo / Pratt), and the Butts part also repeats entry 20.
fix: Drop, or replace with designers not used elsewhere, e.g. parts "Rob Angel's game" (Pictionary) and "Leslie Scott's game" (Jenga).

question: Match each board game to its inventor or original designer.
explanation: The original Game of Life (The Checkered Game of Life, 1860) was designed by Milton Bradley. Reuben Klamer (with Bill Markham) designed the 1960 version, so 'original designer' is debatable. Scrabble and Cluedo also repeat Parts entry 28, and Scrabble repeats entry 20.
fix: Replace the Game of Life pair with "Mastermind" / "Mordecai Meirowitz" and the Scrabble pair with "Trivial Pursuit" / "Chris Haney and Scott Abbott". Do not use Monopoly / Charles Darrow: under 'original designer' Lizzie Magie (The Landlord's Game) is defensible.
